at høre fra.explanation: "At høre fra" means "to hear from". To say someone has not contacted you: "Jeg har ikke hørt fra Mette" (I have not heard from Mette). For news about something, use "at høre om" (to hear about): "Jeg hørte om ulykken" (I heard about the accident).

at høre om.explanation: "At høre om" means "to hear about". To say you learned of an event: "Jeg hørte om branden" (I heard about the fire). To say someone contacted you, use "at høre fra" (to hear from): "Jeg har hørt fra Mette" (I have heard from Mette).

at høre til.explanation: "At høre til" means "to belong". To name the place you belong in, add "i" (in) before the place: "Jeg hører til i Aarhus" (I belong in Aarhus).

at høste.explanation: "At høste" means "to harvest". It is related to "høst" (autumn, the harvest season). To say someone earns praise: "Hun høster ros" (She reaps praise).

en hage.explanation: "En hage" means "a chin". To say someone has a double chin, use "en dobbelthage" (a double chin): "Han har dobbelthage" (He has a double chin). It is also the first part of "en hagesmæk" (a bib).

en hagesmæk.explanation: "En hagesmæk" means "a bib". The first part is "hage" (chin).

en haj.explanation: "En haj" means "a shark". To say a person who lends money at very high interest, use "en lånehaj" (a loan shark): "Han skyldte en lånehaj penge" (He owed a loan shark money).

en hakkebøf.explanation: "En hakkebøf" means "a hamburger steak". It is built from "hakke" (to chop) and "bøf" (steak). In Denmark it is served on a plate with brown gravy, not in a bun.

en hal.explanation: "En hal" means "a hall", as in a large room or building for sports. For the hallway inside a home, use "en gang" (a hallway): "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway).

en hale.explanation: "En hale" means "a tail". The word is also part of "en hestehale" (a ponytail), where "hest" means "horse".

en halmballe.explanation: "En halmballe" means "a straw bale". It is built from "halm" (straw) and "balle" (bale).

en hals.explanation: "En hals" means "a throat / neck". To say you have a sore throat: "Jeg har ondt i halsen" (I have a sore throat). It is also the first part of "en halskæde" (a necklace), where "kæde" means "chain".

en halsbetændelse.explanation: "En halsbetændelse" means "a throat infection". It is built from "hals" (throat) and "betændelse" (infection). For a plain sore throat, say "ondt i halsen" (a sore throat): "Jeg har ondt i halsen" (I have a sore throat).

en halsedisse.explanation: "En halsedisse" means "a neck warmer". The first part is "hals" (neck).

en halskæde.explanation: "En halskæde" means "a necklace". It is built from "hals" (neck) and "kæde" (chain).

en halspastil.explanation: "En halspastil" means "a throat lozenge". It is built from "hals" (throat) and "pastil" (lozenge).

en halv time.explanation: "En halv time" means "half an hour". To say how long something takes: "Det tager en halv time" (It takes half an hour). Do not mix it up with the clock time "halv fem" (4:30): "Vi mødes klokken halv fem" (We meet at half past four).

en halvbror.explanation: "En halvbror" means "a half-brother". It is built from "halv" (half) and "bror" (brother).

en halvdel.explanation: "En halvdel" means "a half". It is built from "halv" (half) and "del" (part). To say half of a thing, put "halv" before the noun: "en halv pizza" (half a pizza).

en halvleg.explanation: "En halvleg" means "a half (of a game)". To say the first half of a match: "første halvleg" (the first half). For one half of a thing you cut, use "en halvdel" (a half): "en halvdel af kagen" (one half of the cake).

en halvsøster.explanation: "En halvsøster" means "a half-sister". It is built from "halv" (half) and "søster" (sister).

en halvø.explanation: "En halvø" means "a peninsula". It is built from "halv" (half) and "ø" (island). For land with water on all sides, use "en ø" (an island): "Fyn er en ø" (Funen is an island).

en hammer.explanation: "En hammer" means "a hammer". To drive in a screw, use "en skruetrækker" (a screwdriver): "Jeg skruer skruen i med en skruetrækker" (I screw the screw in with a screwdriver).

en hamster.explanation: "En hamster" means "a hamster". The verb "at hamstre" (to hoard) comes from it: "Han hamstrer mad" (He hoards food).

en handel.explanation: "En handel" means "a deal". To talk about trading as an activity, leave out "en": "Handel mellem lande er vigtig" (Trade between countries is important).
